llm.summary: The skill mostly does what it says (scans bookmaker odds and writes arb results), but the package name/metadata (mentions Polymarket) and lack of source/homepage are inconsistent with the code which uses The Odds API — this mismatch and missing provenance reduce trust.

dimensions.detail: The skill advertises 'Polymarket Sports Arbitrage' but neither SKILL.md nor the code reference Polymarket or any Polymarket endpoints; instead the code calls The Odds API and uses bookmaker demo data. This naming/metadata mismatch and missing homepage/source make the intended scope unclear even though the implemented functionality (scanning bookmaker odds) is coherent.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The runtime instructions and code are narrowly scoped to fetching odds (The Odds API), computing implied probabilities, logging results to stdout, and appending JSON to a results file (default /tmp/sports_arb_results.json). The skill is configured to run periodically (cron every 30 minutes). Nothing in SKILL.md or the code asks for unrelated system files or secrets, but results are written to a world-readable temporary path by default which could be accessible to other local processes.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: clawhub.json requests a single pip dependency ('requests'), and the code uses requests. There is no arbitrary remote code download or extract step. This is proportionate and expected for a network-fetching Python script.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Only optional environment variables are used (ODDS_API_KEY, MIN_PROFIT_PCT, TOTAL_STAKE, SPORTS, RESULTS_FILE). No unrelated or excessive credentials are requested. The ODDS_API_KEY is optional and the skill falls back to demo data when it is absent.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is an automaton scheduled via clawhub.json (cron: every 30 minutes) and will run periodically while installed. It does not request 'always: true' and does not modify other skills' configurations. Persistent execution increases the importance of provenance and trust in the publisher.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
Things to consider before installing:
- Metadata mismatch: The skill is named 'Polymarket Sports Arbitrage' but the code talks to The Odds API and bookmakers; ask the publisher why the name references Polymarket and request a source/homepage or repo link for verification.
- Provenance: There is no homepage or source repository and the owner ID is unknown. If you don’t trust the publisher, review the included sports_arbitrage.py file yourself before running and verify there are no hidden network calls or data exfiltration paths.
- API key safety: ODDS_API_KEY is optional. If you provide a real API key, it will only be used to call The Odds API, but only provide keys you control and rotate them if you stop using the skill.
- Output file permissions: By default results are written to /tmp/sports_arb_results.json; consider changing RESULTS_FILE to a directory with restricted permissions if you don’t want other local users/processes to read the results.
- Legal/regulatory risk: Automated betting/arbitrage can violate bookmaker terms of service and may have legal/regulatory implications in some jurisdictions — ensure you understand the risks before using outputs to place real bets.
- What would change this assessment: if the publisher provides a verifiable source repository, explains the Polymarket naming, and offers clear provenance, this could be reclassified as benign. As-is, the mismatch and missing provenance justify caution.
